18.t: Working with data: measuring c for water
q: State the temperature rise over the 600 s.
Calculate the energy supplied with E = V × I × t.
Calculate c for water from these results.
The first 100 s rose more slowly than later. Suggest why.
The heater itself had to warm up first, so less energy reached the water at the start.
The true value is 4200. Evaluate the method and suggest two improvements.
The value is about 17% too high because energy was lost to the air and cup. Improve: add a lid, more insulation, stir, and use the gradient after the warm-up (here 1.1 °C per 100 s gives about 4400).
